author: agent
question: Your Claude Code hit its token limit again — what if the real number went down by most of itself?

inspiration.note: Reference = lead only. Their delivery: meme-clip hook, glitch-filter repo reveal, terminal SAVINGS number block as the proof beat, creator head at the end. Taken as principles: hook with the pain state, show a token receipt with real numbers, one tool per beat with its own motion. Their footage, filters, meme inserts and wording stay theirs. Full-video teardown: research/critiques/video-tiktok-vanta-claude-plugins-2026-11-11.md

steps: CLAUDE CODE TOKEN LIMIT: FOUR FIXES
FOUR FREE PLUGINS · NOT BY ANTHROPIC
hook_visual.intent: the limit state first: a red usage bar pinned at the top edge, four plugin names struck in underneath, the count ticking down — the pain is on screen before any name is said

points.claim: Headroom compresses tool output, logs, files and RAG chunks before the model reads them — sixty to ninety-five percent fewer tokens on JSON, roughly fifteen to twenty percent on coding-agent turns, local-first and reversible.
points.spoken: Headroom compresses everything your agent reads — tool output, logs, files — before the model sees it. Ninety-eight percent saved on one real task. It is reversible.
points.source_note: cherylaurelia/headroom README: '60 to 95 percent fewer tokens for JSON', about 15-20 percent on coding-agent turns, local-first and reversible. The ninety-eight percent figure is the maintainer's single demo run, not a benchmark — say 'one real task', not 'in general'.

visual.intent: compressed-context visual: a fat JSON blob squeezes into a thin chip as the token counter spins down to a small number; a green receipt stamp lands — the tool's own terminal on screen, house heading and captions over it

points.title: INPUT, BEFORE IT IS READ
points.sub: Headroom compresses tool output, logs and files before the model reads them.

points.claim: Ponytail makes the agent write far less code — its own benchmarks claim roughly fifty-four percent less code and about twenty percent cheaper API cost.
points.spoken: Ponytail stops your agent writing ten lines where two work. Its own benchmark says fifty-four percent less code — and output tokens are the expensive ones.
points.source_note: digicuratoragency round-up: Ponytail's own benchmark claims about 54 percent less code and roughly 20 percent cheaper calls. Vendor-reported — the plan says 'its own benchmark' out loud.

visual.intent: two code blocks side by side: the left is a wall of text, the right is four lines, scissors sweep, a price tag stamps the saving — the tool's own editor on screen, house heading and captions over it

points.title: OUTPUT, BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN
points.sub: Ponytail's own benchmark: fifty-four percent less code, about twenty percent cheaper.
steps: Its own benchmark, not a lab

points.claim: OmniRoute reroutes agent traffic to free model providers the moment the usage limit hits, claiming about one and a half billion free tokens a month across hundreds of providers; Graphify maps the codebase once locally so agents stop re-reading the same files.
points.spoken: When the limit still comes, OmniRoute switches you to free models mid-session. Graphify maps your codebase once — the agent stops re-reading it.
points.source_note: digicuratoragency round-up: OmniRoute advertises roughly 1.47 billion free tokens a month across 352 providers; Graphify builds a local codebase map once. The free-provider count is OmniRoute's own claim.

visual.intent: network router graphic: a red blocked lane flips to a green free lane mid-frame; then a map of the codebase lights up once and stays lit — the tool's own router on screen, house heading and captions over it

points.title: ROUTE AROUND THE LIMIT
points.sub: OmniRoute reroutes to free models; Graphify maps your codebase once, locally.
steps: Free providers when the limit hits
No more re-reading the same files
